model: IMMP-BAC(A) BACnet gateway - indoor unit device
applies_to: Midea MDV VRF and commercial indoor units connected through the IMMP-BAC(A) building control gateway.
summary: The IMMP-BAC(A) (K05.2-BACNET(A)) is a Midea building control gateway that publishes every connected VRF indoor unit, outdoor unit and HTHM hydronic module as its own BACnet IP device. This is the object set of one indoor unit device: on/off, mode, fan speed, setpoints and lock commands plus room, coil and discharge temperatures and the error code.
notes: The manual is in Spanish (Midea Spain); object names are kept as printed and the English descriptions are ours.

Each unit is its own BACnet device. Indoor unit device instance = BACnet network number x 10000 + RS-485 port (0-3) x 1000 + indoor address (0-63); outdoor unit = network x 10000 + port x 1000 + 100 + outdoor address (0-31).
Some models do not support every object (for example cooling-only systems have no heat or auto mode).
Error codes are numbered 1-260 and map to the display codes A0...UU (blocks of 20 per letter).
The doc marks objects L (read) or L/E (read and write the unit state); there is no priority-array information.

integration.summary: Give the gateway an IP address and a BACnet network number, then discover one BACnet device per indoor unit. Map BV 1 on/off, MV 1 mode, MV 2 fan speed and AV 1 setpoint, and read AI 1 room temperature, BI 2 alarm and AI 7 error code.
setup: Default gateway IP address is 192.168.1.8; change it on the gateway web page, then set a BACnet network number between 2 and 254 (unique per gateway) and restart the gateway for it to take effect.
Unit device instances follow the network/port/address formula in the notes.
gotchas: Space commands at least 200 ms apart or the gateway can drop them.
When BV 1 turns a unit on it resumes its last mode, fan and setpoint; a unit seen off at first connection defaults to cooling 24 °C, fan speed 1.
In AUTO mode AV 2 must be at or above AV 3; the gateway raises AV 2 to match if not.
On 3-speed fans, MV 2 values 1-2 = low, 3-4 = medium, 5-7 = high.
